dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi, yes, good afternoon. I'm calling about standing water at a crosswalk. I'm at 136 Marsh Street, down The Point. Can you hear me okay? I've got one bar here.
I can hear you fine. A little bit of an echo, but go ahead. 136 Marsh Street, in The Point. And what's going on there?

So since last weekend's nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday, there's water pooled across the crosswalk right by the school bus stop. It's the one at the corner near my place. The storm drain there doesn't seem to be taking anything. It's just sitting.
Okay. So the water is sitting across the crosswalk by the bus stop, and it's been that way since the storm. Is it the whole width of the crosswalk?

Pretty much the whole thing, curb to curb on my side. The kids are waiting for the bus in the morning and they're stepping off into the road to get around it. [line breaks up] ...cars coming through, so that's the part I don't love.
You broke up on me for a second. You said the kids are stepping into the road to get around the water, and cars are coming through. Is that right?
Yes, correct. They step out past the edge of the puddle, into the travel lane. Nobody's been hit, but it's a matter of time with how people take that corner.
Understood. And is it just water, or is there anything else on the sidewalk?

The sidewalk is a sheet of mud and grit. When the water came up it left all this sand and silt, and now it's slick. You can't really walk on it without sliding, so that's pushing the kids toward the road even more.
Okay, mud and grit left over on the sidewalk, slick. Let me write that down. Do you know if the drain itself is blocked with debris, or can you see the grate?
I can see the grate. It's got leaves and a bunch of gravel packed on top. I didn't touch it. I didn't want to be out there in the road messing with it.
No, you shouldn't. That's good. Leaves and gravel packed on the grate. Is the water still deep, or has it gone down at all since Sunday?

It's gone down some. It was probably four, five inches Sunday. Now it's maybe two at the deepest. But it's not draining, it's just evaporating or soaking in. And we're supposed to get more rain this weekend, I think.
Okay. So down some, but still standing, and more weather possibly coming. I'll put that in as well. Can I get a name and a good callback number?
Teresa Amaral. Number is 401-555-0175.
Teresa Amaral, 401-555-0175. Did I get that right?
Yep, that's it.
And the cross street there, is it near the school, or is the school a block over?
[inaudible] ...the bus stop, not the school itself. The school's a few blocks. It's the stop at the corner just down from my house on Marsh. I'm at 136, and it's the next corner toward the water.
Sorry, the line cut out. The bus stop is at the corner just down from 136 Marsh, toward the water?
Yes. Toward the water side, next corner.
Got it. I'm going to send this over to the crew that handles drains and catch basins. Because of the kids and the road, I'll flag it as a safety concern so it doesn't just sit in the queue.
Appreciate that. Can I ask, do the crews work on weekends? Because if it's going to rain again I'd rather it be cleared before then.

Sometimes they do, especially after a storm when there's a backlog. I can't tell you for sure whether someone will be out on this one on a weekend. What I can do is put the request in today and note the timing concern with the forecast.
Okay. That works. So it goes in today, and somebody will call me?

It goes in today. Whether you hear back by phone or just see a crew out there, I can't say which, but you have the number on the ticket either way. If it gets worse or the water spreads, call back and we'll add to it.
Fine. And if it's not cleared by Friday, I call back and reference the same ticket?

Yes, just give your address and say you called Wednesday about the bus stop crosswalk. I'll make sure the note says that. Let me read it back to you. Standing water across the crosswalk at the bus stop near 136 Marsh Street, The Point. Storm drain grate covered in leaves and gravel. Sidewalk covered in mud and grit. Children stepping into the roadway. Caller Teresa Amaral, 401-555-0175. Anything to fix?

No, that's right. Oh, and one other thing, totally unrelated. I'm looking for a particular size of lightbulb, and I was trying to figure out if the city handles streetlight bulbs or if that's something else. The streetlight there is out too, now that I think of it.
Streetlights, I'd have to check which office. Is the light out at that same corner?

Same corner, yes. Actually, I mean, I was thinking of a lightbulb for my own porch, a specific size. I got mixed up. I'll just go to the hardware store for that. But the streetlight at the corner has been out since the storm, I think.

Okay, the porch bulb is a hardware store thing. For the streetlight, I'll add a note to the ticket that it's out at that corner, and I'll mention it to whoever handles lighting. Do you know if there's a pole number? Usually there's a little tag on the pole.
I'd have to go look. I can check when I walk the dog later and call it in if there's a number.
That would help. If there's no tag, the description is enough. Corner by the bus stop, near 136 Marsh.
Great. Okay, that's everything I needed.
All right, Teresa. Thanks for calling it in. Hopefully somebody gets out there soon.
Thanks. Have a good afternoon.
You too. Bye now.
